message.content: Read redu.md and deploy Centrifugo on redu.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- amazon-bedrock: Builds generative AI applications on Amazon Bedrock. Covers model invocation (Converse API, InvokeModel), RAG with Knowledge Bases, Bedrock Agents, Guardrails, and AgentCore. Use when invoking models, setting up Knowledge Bases, creating agents, applying guardrails, deploying to AgentCore, troubleshooting Bedrock errors (ThrottlingException, AccessDeniedException), or choosing models (Claude, Llama, [infra], Titan). ALSO USE for prompt caching setup and debugging, quota health checks and throttling diagnosis, cost attribution and tracking, migrating between Claude model generations (4.5 to 4.6 to 4.7), chunking strategies, API selection (Converse vs InvokeModel), guardrail capabilities, and model selection. Also covers AgentCore Payments setup (x402, microtransactions, Payment Manager, Connector, Instrument, Coinbase CDP, Stripe Privy, 402 Payment Required, pay for content, paid endpoint, agent payments). NOT for custom model training, Rekognition, or Comprehend.
- aws-billing-and-cost-management: Analyze AWS costs, find savings, manage budgets, evaluate Savings Plans and Reserved Instances, right-size EC2/Lambda/RDS/EBS with Compute Optimizer, look up service pricing, query CUR with Athena, detect cost anomalies, scope costs to billing views, and monitor Free Tier usage. Triggers on: AWS bill, cost analysis, reduce spend, savings plan, reserved instance, right-size, budget alert, cost optimization, pricing, free tier, cost anomaly, CUR, cost audit, billing view, billing view ARN.
- aws-blocks: Guides building full-stack applications with AWS Blocks — an Infrastructure-from-Code framework. Applies when creating APIs, selecting Building Blocks (KVStore, DistributedTable, Database, AuthBasic, AuthCognito, Realtime, AsyncJob, FileBucket, etc.), running local development, or deploying AWS Blocks applications. Also covers AWS Blocks topics with validated, version-specific patterns that prevent common mistakes. Triggers when user mentions AWS Blocks; project has aws-blocks/ directory; code imports @aws-blocks packages.
- aws-cdk: Authors, deploys, and troubleshoots AWS infrastructure using CDK with TypeScript or Python. Covers best practices, stack architecture, and construct patterns. Always use when writing CDK constructs, bootstrapping environments, running cdk deploy/synth/diff, fixing CDK or CloudFormation errors, planning stack structure, importing existing resources, resolving drift, or refactoring stacks without resource replacement.
- aws-cloudformation: Author, validate, and troubleshoot AWS CloudFormation templates. Covers template authoring with secure defaults, pre-deployment validation (cfn-lint, cfn-guard, change sets), and root-cause diagnosis of failed stacks using CloudFormation events and CloudTrail correlation.
- aws-containers: Deploys and operates containerized workloads on ECS, Fargate, and ECR. Covers task definitions, Fargate services, ECR repository setup and lifecycle policies, ECS Exec debugging, service scaling, deployment strategies, load balancer integration, and logging configuration. Use when deploying, debugging, or optimizing containers on AWS. ALSO USE for container deployment options (ECS vs ECS Express Mode), networking modes, health check troubleshooting, OOM errors, secrets injection, blue/green deployments, ECR image management, and App Runner sunset guidance and migration. NOT for Kubernetes, EKS, or CI/CD pipelines.
- aws-messaging-and-streaming: Guides use of AWS messaging and streaming services. Covers Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon MQ, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, and Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK). Use when implementing messaging and streaming patterns.
- aws-observability: Builds, configures, debugs, and optimizes AWS observability with CloudWatch (Log Insights, Metrics, Alarms, Dashboards, EMF), X-Ray, CloudTrail, and ADOT (AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry), AND enables/onboards services to Application Signals using ADOT auto-instrumentation SDKs. Covers Log Insights queries, alarms (metric, composite, anomaly), dashboards, custom metrics/EMF, X-Ray tracing and sampling, ADOT collector config, CloudTrail auditing, and end-to-end Application Signals enablement via ADOT SDKs (CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on, CloudWatch Agent IAM, OTLP endpoints, ServiceEvents, Dynamic Instrumentation), breakpoint and snapshot in Dynamic Instrumentation, live data capture in running service, debug without redeploying. Applies to CloudWatch, alarms, dashboards, EMF, X-Ray, traces, CloudTrail,  ADOT, monitoring, synthetics/canaries, OR enabling/onboarding/instrumenting a service for Application Signals. Not for app logging or security threat detection.
- aws-sdk-js-v3-usage: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 development patterns. Use when writing JavaScript or TypeScript code that uses AWS services via @aws-sdk/* packages (aws-sdk-js-v3), or when asked about schemas, runtime validation, serialization, or code generation in the context of the JS/TS AWS SDK.
- aws-sdk-python-usage: AWS SDK for Python (boto3/botocore) development patterns. You MUST use this skill when writing Python code that uses AWS services via boto3 or botocore. This includes creating service clients or resources, configuring sessions and credentials, handling errors with ClientError, using paginators and waiters, S3 file transfers and presigned URLs, DynamoDB table operations, and any boto3/botocore client configuration. Use this skill whenever Python code imports boto3 or botocore, or when the user asks about AWS operations in Python.
- aws-sdk-swift-usage: AWS SDK for Swift development patterns. Use when writing Swift code that uses AWS services via aws-sdk-swift package.
- aws-serverless: Builds, deploys, manages, debugs, configures, and optimizes serverless applications on AWS using Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, EventBridge, and SAM/CDK. Covers cold starts, CORS debugging, event source mappings, troubleshooting, concurrency, SnapStart, Powertools, function URLs, EventBridge Scheduler, Lambda layers, and production readiness. Triggers on mentions of Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, SAM templates, CDK serverless stacks, DynamoDB stream triggers, SQS event sources, cold starts, timeouts, 502/504 errors, throttling, concurrency, CORS, Powertools, or any event-driven architecture on AWS, even without the word "serverless." Does not apply to EC2, ECS/Fargate containers, or Amplify hosting.
- cso: Chief Security Officer mode. (gstack)
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- investigate: Systematic debugging with root cause investigation. (gstack)
- office-hours: YC Office Hours — two modes. (gstack)
- review: Pre-landing PR review. (gstack)
- signing-in-to-aws: Gets AWS credentials for CLI/SDK access via `aws login`. Activates when a developer needs to authenticate to AWS for local development, when an AWS operation fails due to missing or expired credentials, or when someone asks about setting up AWS access. Triggers: "set up AWS", "configure AWS", "aws login", "get credentials", "authenticate", "session expired", "token expired", "no credentials", "AccessDeniedException" with no configured credentials.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	---
2	redu_schema: 2
3	repo: https://github.com/centrifugal/centrifugo
4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: centrifugo/centrifugo:v6.9.1
7	  port: 8000
8	  vm: m1.small
9	  flavor_id: "2"
10	  database: none. Centrifugo's default engine is in-memory; do not provision one
11	  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0174
12	bootstrap:
13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: centrifugo
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: NOBODY, BECAUSE CENTRIFUGO HAS NO USER ACCOUNTS AT ALL. There is no signup form, no install wizard and no first-visitor race, and that IS the ownership answer for this app. The only privileged surface is the admin web UI, and it is guarded by a single password plus a token-signing secret that YOU set at deploy time from environment variables (internal/configtypes/types.go:609-621). That is the deploy-time case, the one that is safe by construction. Two consequences: there is no window to close after boot, and there is also nobody to recover the password from, so record it with the user at handover."
18	  - "⛔⛔⛔ NEVER SET admin.insecure, http_api.insecure OR client.insecure ON A PUBLIC HOSTNAME, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT ENDS BADLY. internal/admin/handlers.go:62-70: when admin.insecure is true the auth middleware returns the handler UNWRAPPED, so every admin endpoint including POST /admin/api is open to the internet. /admin/api is the full server API: publish into any channel, disconnect any user, read history and presence. The equivalents are http_api.insecure (drops the API key check, internal/app/mux.go:259-260) and client.insecure (accepts every client connection as anonymous, internal/configtypes/types.go:471). All three exist for a laptop on localhost. Every tutorial that shows them is talking about a laptop. Leave all three FALSE, and never set client.token.insecure_skip_token_signature_verify either."
19	  - "⛔ SET admin.password AND admin.secret TOGETHER, OR THE UI IS DEAD RATHER THAN OPEN. Verified in internal/admin/handlers.go:73-77 and 139-143: an empty secret makes every admin request 401 with \"no admin secret key found in configuration\" in the log, and an empty password OR secret makes POST /admin/auth answer 400 with \"admin_password and admin_secret must be set in configuration\". So Centrifugo fails CLOSED, which is the good news, and the bad news is that it looks exactly like a broken deployment. Generate both (`openssl rand -hex 32` each), set CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_ENABLED, CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_SECRET, and prove the login works with the script in the body of this file rather than assuming."
20	  - "⛔ THE ADMIN UI, THE HTTP API AND HEALTH ARE ALL ON THE SAME PORT AS THE WEBSOCKET, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE HERE. internal/app/mux.go:390-393: if http_server.internal_port is empty, Centrifugo reuses the main port for the internal endpoints. Upstream's advice for a datacentre is to set a separate internal port and firewall it; on redu that would put the admin UI and the API on a port NOTHING proxies, and you would have deployed an unreachable control plane. So LEAVE internal_port UNSET, accept that /admin and /api are on the public hostname, and treat CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY and CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD as the only things standing between the internet and your message bus. Both fail closed when empty, but empty is not a security posture."
21	  - "⛔ SET client.allowed_origins OR EVERY BROWSER IS REFUSED WHILE EVERYTHING ELSE LOOKS FINE. internal/app/origin.go:16-26: with the list EMPTY, Centrifugo allows only requests that carry NO Origin header. Browsers always send one, so every browser WebSocket handshake is rejected and the only evidence is an info-level log line, \"request Origin is not authorized due to empty allowed_origins\". Server-side clients send no Origin and connect happily, which is what makes this look like the browser's fault. Set it to the exact origins of the apps that will connect. ⚠️ THE SEPARATOR IS A SPACE, NOT A COMMA (internal/config/envconfig/envconfig.go:270 sets SliceSep to a single space), so CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS should read like \"https://app.example.com https://staging.example.com\". A comma-separated value becomes ONE nonsense origin and every browser stays refused. Using * works and logs a warning; prefer the exact list."
22	  - "⛔ THE SECRETS ARE THE WHOLE PRODUCT, AND A REDEPLOY THAT REGENERATES THEM BREAKS YOUR BACKEND SILENTLY ON CENTRIFUGO'S SIDE. There is no database here, so nothing local is lost, and that is exactly why this is easy to miss: (1) CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_TOKEN_HMAC_SECRET_KEY verifies every connection JWT your backend mints (internal/configtypes/types.go:53-54). Change it and every existing token is rejected and every client fails to connect. (2) CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY is what your backend sends on every publish. Change it and every publish starts answering 401 while the realtime layer stays up, so your app looks alive and stops updating. (3) CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_SECRET signs admin sessions. Generate all three ONCE, store them with the user, and pass the SAME values on every redeploy."
23	  - "NO DATABASE. DO NOT PROVISION ONE. engine.type defaults to \"memory\" (internal/configtypes/engine.go:5), so a single-node Centrifugo keeps channel history and presence in RAM and needs nothing else. That is why this is the cheapest possible entry: one m1.small VM and no second machine on the bill. The honest cost of that default: history and presence are LOST on every restart and every redeploy, and you cannot run two Centrifugo nodes. Both are fixed the same way, by pointing engine.type at redis, which on redu means a managed Redis and roughly GBP 0.0174/hr more. That changes the quote, so it is the user's decision, not yours. Say it up front rather than after the first restart."
24	  - "PORT 8000, from internal/configtypes/types.go:18. Pass 8000 to deploy_compose. Health check: set CENTRIFUGO_HEALTH_ENABLED=true (it defaults to FALSE, internal/configtypes/types.go:375) and probe GET /health, which returns the literal two-character JSON body {} (internal/health/health.go:27-30). ⚠️ That body is a terrible thing to assert on by itself, since almost any JSON endpoint could produce it. Assert on GET /admin/init instead, which returns edition and insecure fields that only Centrifugo serves."
25	  - "⛔ DO NOT USE THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE. IT IS A TEST HARNESS AND IT DOES NOT CONTAIN CENTRIFUGO. centrifugal/centrifugo's docker-compose.yml starts nats, postgres, a streaming postgres replica that WIPES ITSELF on every restart (its own comment says so), a Google Pub/Sub emulator, localstack, redpanda, kafka and redis, all for integration tests against consumers. There is no centrifugo service in it. misc/clickhouse_cluster/docker-compose.yml is likewise for the PRO analytics feature. Write the one-service compose in the body of this file instead, pulling centrifugo/centrifugo:v6.9.1. Never :latest: the tag exists and a redeploy across a release would change the app under the user."
26	  - "CONFIGURE IT WITH ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES, NOT A CONFIG FILE, AND KNOW THE NAMING RULE. The image looks for ./config.json in /centrifugo and, not finding one, logs \"config file not found, continue using environment and flag options\" and carries on (internal/app/cmd.go:18, internal/app/run.go:66-67). That warning is EXPECTED with this recipe and is not an error. Env names are CENTRIFUGO_ plus the config path with dots replaced by underscores, uppercased: http_server.port becomes CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_SERVER_PORT, client.token.hmac_secret_key becomes CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_TOKEN_HMAC_SECRET_KEY, http_api.key becomes CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY. Note http_server, not http."
27	  - "A TYPO IN A VARIABLE NAME IS A WARNING, NOT A FAILURE, SO GREP FOR IT. internal/config/config.go:226 collects every CENTRIFUGO_* variable it does not recognise and internal/app/log.go:32-34 logs each as \"unknown var in environment\". Nothing fails. So a misspelled CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD leaves the admin UI unusable with no obvious cause. After boot check BOTH halves: `sudo docker logs <container> | grep -c 'starting Centrifugo'` must be at least 1, which is what proves your command reached the container at all, and only then `sudo docker logs <container> | grep 'unknown var in environment'` must be empty. A zero from the second grep means nothing unless the first one is non-zero."
28	  - "⛔ ANONYMOUS CONNECTIONS ARE OFF BY DEFAULT, KEEP THEM THAT WAY. client.allow_anonymous_connect_without_token defaults to false (internal/configtypes/types.go:428), so a client that presents no JWT is refused. That is correct: Centrifugo's entire authorisation model is the token your backend signs, which carries the user id and the channels they may subscribe to. Turning it on makes every channel that is not otherwise protected readable by anyone who can reach the hostname. If the user genuinely wants a public broadcast channel, that is a per-namespace decision in the channel config, not a global flag."
29	  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, with this recipe: GET / serves the admin single-page app, which is static assets and no data; GET /admin/init returns {\"insecure\":false,\"edition\":\"oss\",\"authenticated\":false} and nothing more; GET /health returns {}; POST /admin/api and POST /api both answer 401 without a token or key; and the WebSocket endpoint refuses a connection with no JWT. Nothing else is registered, because prometheus, swagger and the pprof debug handler all default to false (internal/configtypes/types.go:356, 380, 385) and this recipe leaves them there. Do not enable /metrics on the public port without thinking about what it exposes."
30	  - "NO VOLUME AND NO PERSISTENT STATE. The container writes nothing it needs to keep: no database, no uploads, no config file with this recipe. That makes a redeploy genuinely stateless, and it is also why the secrets above must be recorded outside the deployment. If you later switch to a config file, mount it read-only and remember the container runs as uid 1000 (Dockerfile, USER centrifugo)."
31	  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED, and no first-boot setup step at all. The binary starts and serves. That is unusual in this library and worth saying out loud: if the URL answers and the admin login works, the deploy is finished."
32	  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO NUMBER IN THE REPO. It is a single static Go binary on alpine with an in-memory broker, so m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is a reasonable floor and makes this the cheapest shape in the library at one VM and no database. ⚠️ The estimate is per-connection-count, not per-app: memory here scales with concurrent connections, their message queues (client.queue_max_size defaults to 1 MB per connection as a CEILING, not an allocation) and retained channel history. A few thousand idle connections is a different machine from a few hundred. Measure it on your run and write the real number back."
33	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (GBP 0.0174/hr, about GBP 12.70 a month, NO managed database, inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), no database, port 8000. ⚠️ plan_deploy upsizes a compose stack to m1.large once needs_compose is declared; pass flavor_id explicitly to hold m1.small, because that larger floor exists for apps that BUILD from source and this one is a pulled static binary."
34	  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built. Write the one-service compose locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the Centrifugo repository would pick up the integration-test compose described above and start eight containers that have nothing to do with the app."
35	  - "WEBSOCKETS WORK THROUGH redu's PROXY, and you do not have to do anything to make that true: redu creates every proxy host with websocket upgrade enabled. Clients connect to wss://<your-host>/connection/websocket. If you want the SSE or HTTP-streaming fallbacks for networks that block WebSocket, they are separate handlers and both default to DISABLED (internal/configtypes/types.go:110, 117); enabling them also registers the /emulation endpoint automatically (internal/app/mux.go:418-421)."
36	  - "LICENCE: Apache 2.0, verified from the LICENSE file itself, 202 lines, Copyright 2023 Centrifugal Labs LTD, unmodified and with no network clause. ⚠️ awesome-selfhosted's metadata says MIT and is WRONG. Note also that Centrifugo PRO is a separate commercial product: the OSS build reports edition \"oss\" on /admin/init, and nothing in this recipe enables or requires PRO."
37	  - "DELETING IT TAKES EVERYTHING WITH IT, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF MOST ENTRIES HERE. There is no managed database left behind and no residual bill, because there was never a second machine. There is also no history to recover: with the memory engine, channel history and presence exist only in the running process. Say that plainly before deleting, and remember that every client and backend still pointed at the old hostname will simply stop connecting."
38	---
39	
40	# Self-host Centrifugo on redu
41	
42	A real-time messaging server you own: WebSocket connections, channels, presence and history, with

49	- **No database.** The default engine keeps channel history and presence in memory, so there is
50	  nothing else to provision and nothing else on the bill.
51	- The admin web UI, the HTTP API and the WebSocket endpoint on one public hostname, with the
52	  admin password, the admin secret and the API key all set at deploy time.

67	
68	**Centrifugo has no user accounts.** No signup form, no install wizard, no first-visitor race.
69	The only privileged surface is the admin UI, and it is guarded by a password and a token-signing
70	secret that are set from environment variables before the container ever starts. That is the
71	deploy-time case, which is the only one that is safe by construction.
72	
73	What that leaves you responsible for is the four secrets, since nothing on the server can
74	regenerate or recover them:
75	
76	| Variable | What it protects |
77	|---|---|
78	| `CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | the admin web UI |
79	| `CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_SECRET` | the tokens that UI issues to itself |
80	| `CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY` | the server API your backend publishes through |

93	    ports:

96	      CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_SERVER_PORT: "8000"
97	      CENTRIFUGO_HEALTH_ENABLED: "true"

101	      CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_INSECURE: "false"

119	## Verify it, and prove the insecure flags are actually off
120	
121	```bash
122	#!/usr/bin/env bash
123	# Verify a Centrifugo deploy. Exit 0 pass, 1 fail, 3 inconclusive.
124	# Usage: ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] API_KEY=[REDACTED:value] ./verify.sh centrifugo-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
125	if [ "$#" -lt 1 ]; then
126	  echo "usage: ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] API_KEY=[REDACTED:value] $0 <centrifugo-host.redu.cloud>" >&2
127	  exit 2
128	fi
129	HOST=$1
130	INCONCLUSIVE=3
131	if [ -z "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" ] || [ -z "$API_KEY" ]; then
132	  echo "set ADMIN_PASSWORD and API_KEY in the environment, not on the command line" >&2
133	  exit 2
134	fi
135	TMP=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
136	trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
137	
138	# (1) Is it Centrifugo answering, or redu's proxy while the container starts? /admin/init is the
139	# only endpoint that returns something nothing else could return.
140	code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/init" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/admin/init")
141	if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
142	  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the container is still starting. Re-run shortly." >&2
143	  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
144	fi
145	if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
146	  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP $code on /admin/init. If it is 404, the admin UI is disabled." >&2
147	  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
148	fi
149	if ! grep -qF '"edition"' "$TMP/init"; then
150	  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP 200 but the body is not a Centrifugo admin init response." >&2
151	  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
152	fi
153	
154	# (2) The security assertion, in the SAME body that just proved we are talking to Centrifugo,
155	# so it cannot go vacuous. insecure true means every admin endpoint is unauthenticated.
156	if grep -qF '"insecure":true' "$TMP/init"; then
157	  echo "FAIL: admin.insecure is ON. Every admin endpoint is open to the internet." >&2
158	  echo "Take this instance down now, unset CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_INSECURE and redeploy." >&2
159	  exit 1
160	fi
161	if ! grep -qF '"insecure":false' "$TMP/init"; then
162	  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /admin/init reported neither insecure true nor false." >&2
163	  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
164	fi
165	
166	# (3) The admin password WORKS, not merely that it was set. Body in a file, never in argv.
167	printf 'password=[REDACTED:value]' "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" > "$TMP/body"
168	curl -sS -X POST -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary "@$TMP/body" "https://$HOST/admin/auth" > "$TMP/auth"
169	ADMIN_TOKEN=«REDACTED:assigned:6d257615» -o '"token":"[REDACTED:value]"]*"' "$TMP/auth" | cut -d'"' -f4)
170	if [ -z "$ADMIN_TOKEN" ]; then
171	  echo "FAIL: /admin/auth returned no token. A 400 here means the password or the secret is" >&2
172	  echo "empty; anything else means the password is wrong." >&2
173	  cat "$TMP/auth" >&2
174	  exit 1
175	fi
176	echo "OK: admin login works."
177	
178	# (4) The API key WORKS. The header goes in a curl config file, not in argv where ps shows it.
179	printf 'header = "X-API-Key: %s"' "$API_KEY" > "$TMP/curlrc"
180	withkey=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/info" -w '%{http_code}' -K "$TMP/curlrc" -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{}' "https://$HOST/api/info")
181	if [ "$withkey" = "404" ]; then
182	  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/info answered 404, so the route moved in this build and the check" >&2
183	  echo "below proves nothing. Do NOT leave this instance running until you re-verify by hand." >&2
184	  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
185	fi
186	if [ "$withkey" != "200" ] || ! grep -qF '"result"' "$TMP/info"; then
187	  echo "FAIL: the API key did not work against /api/info (HTTP $withkey)." >&2
188	  exit 1
189	fi
190	echo "OK: the HTTP API accepts the key and /api/info returned a result."
191	
192	# (5) Only NOW the negative: the same route must refuse an anonymous call. Step 4 is what makes
193	# this meaningful, because it already proved the route exists and is reachable.
194	nokey=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{}' "https://$HOST/api/info")
195	if [ "$nokey" != "401" ]; then
196	  echo "FAIL: /api/info answered $nokey without an API key, expected 401. The server API is" >&2
197	  echo "OPEN. Check CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY and CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_INSECURE." >&2
198	  exit 1
199	fi
200	
201	echo "OK: the API refuses an anonymous call (401), admin.insecure is off, and the admin"
202	echo "password and API key both work."
203	```

205	## The three that actually break it
206	
207	**The empty origin list.** Leave `client.allowed_origins` unset and every browser handshake is
208	refused while server-side clients connect fine. The separator is a **space**, not a comma.
209

211	off a whole authentication layer. They exist for a laptop. On a public hostname any one of them
212	is total compromise.
213	
214	**The internal port.** Upstream tells you to split the admin UI and API onto a separate internal
215	port and firewall it. On redu that would put your control plane on a port nothing proxies. Leave
216	it unset, and let the API key and admin password do the work.

## What this deploys

- **Centrifugo** from the official image, pinned to `v6.9.1`, on one m1.small VM, port 8000.
- **No database.** The default engine keeps channel history and presence in memory, so there is
  nothing else to provision and nothing else on the bill.

What that leaves you responsible for is the four secrets, since nothing on the server can

| Variable | What it protects |
|---|---|

```bash
HOST=$1
INCONCLUSIVE=3
if [ -z "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" ] || [ -z "$API_KEY" ]; then
  echo "set ADMIN_PASSWORD and API_KEY in the environment, not on the command line" >&2
  exit 2
fi
TMP=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# (1) Is it Centrifugo answering, or redu's proxy while the container starts? /admin/init is the
# only endpoint that returns something nothing else could return.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/init" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/admin/init")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the container is still starting. Re-run shortly." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP $code on /admin/init. If it is 404, the admin UI is disabled." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if ! grep -qF '"edition"' "$TMP/init"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP 200 but the body is not a Centrifugo admin init response." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi

# (2) The security assertion, in the SAME body that just proved we are talking to Centrifugo,
# so it cannot go vacuous. insecure true means every admin endpoint is unauthenticated.
if grep -qF '"insecure":true' "$TMP/init"; then
  echo "FAIL: admin.insecure is ON. Every admin endpoint is open to the internet." >&2
  echo "Take this instance down now, unset CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_INSECURE and redeploy." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -qF '"insecure":false' "$TMP/init"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /admin/init reported neither insecure true nor false." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi

# (3) The admin password WORKS, not merely that it was set. Body in a file, never in argv.
printf 'password=[REDACTED:value]' "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" > "$TMP/body"
curl -sS -X POST -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary "@$TMP/body" "https://$HOST/admin/auth" > "$TMP/auth"
ADMIN_TOKEN=«REDACTED:assigned:6d257615» -o '"token":"[REDACTED:value]"]*"' "$TMP/auth" | cut -d'"' -f4)
if [ -z "$ADMIN_TOKEN" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: /admin/auth returned no token. A 400 here means the password or the secret is" >&2
  echo "empty; anything else means the password is wrong." >&2
  cat "$TMP/auth" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: admin login works."

# (4) The API key WORKS. The header goes in a curl config file, not in argv where ps shows it.
printf 'header = "X-API-Key: %s"' "$API_KEY" > "$TMP/curlrc"
withkey=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/info" -w '%{http_code}' -K "$TMP/curlrc" -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{}' "https://$HOST/api/info")
if [ "$withkey" = "404" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/info answered 404, so the route moved in this build and the check" >&2
  echo "below proves nothing. Do NOT leave this instance running until you re-verify by hand." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$withkey" != "200" ] || ! grep -qF '"result"' "$TMP/info"; then
  echo "FAIL: the API key did not work against /api/info (HTTP $withkey)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: the HTTP API accepts the key and /api/info returned a result."

# (5) Only NOW the negative: the same route must refuse an anonymous call. Step 4 is what makes
# this meaningful, because it already proved the route exists and is reachable.
nokey=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{}' "https://$HOST/api/info")
if [ "$nokey" != "401" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: /api/info answered $nokey without an API key, expected 401. The server API is" >&2
  echo "OPEN. Check CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY and CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_INSECURE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "OK: the API refuses an anonymous call (401), admin.insecure is off, and the admin"
echo "password and API key both work."
```

## The three that actually break it

**The empty origin list.** Leave `client.allowed_origins` unset and every browser handshake is
refused while server-side clients connect fine. The separator is a **space**, not a comma.

**The insecure flags.** `admin.insecure`, `http_api.insecure` and `client.insecure` each turn
off a whole authentication layer. They exist for a laptop. On a public hostname any one of them
is total compromise.

**The internal port.** Upstream tells you to split the admin UI and API onto a separate internal
port and firewall it. On redu that would put your control plane on a port nothing proxies. Leave
it unset, and let the API key and admin password do the work.

---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/centrifugal/centrifugo
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: centrifugo/centrifugo:v6.9.1
  port: 8000
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: none. Centrifugo's default engine is in-memory; do not provision one
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0174
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: centrifugo
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: NOBODY, BECAUSE CENTRIFUGO HAS NO USER ACCOUNTS AT ALL. There is no signup form, no install wizard and no first-visitor race, and that IS the ownership answer for this app. The only privileged surface is the admin web UI, and it is guarded by a single password plus a token-signing secret that YOU set at deploy time from environment variables (internal/configtypes/types.go:609-621). That is the deploy-time case, the one that is safe by construction. # Self-host Centrifugo on redu

A real-time messaging server you own: WebSocket connections, channels, presence and history, with
your backend publishing over an HTTP API. One small Go container, no database, and a public
HTTPS URL with TLS.

## What this deploys

- **Centrifugo** from the official image, pinned to `v6.9.1`, on one m1.small VM, port 8000.
- **No database.** The default engine keeps channel history and presence in memory, so there is
  nothing else to provision and nothing else on the bill.
- The admin web UI, the HTTP API and the WebSocket endpoint on one public hostname, with the
  admin password, the admin secret and the API key all set at deploy time.

GBP 0.0174/hour, about GBP 12.70 a month. The cheapest shape in this library, and inside the
no-card free trial.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Centrifugo on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## How ownership works here, because it is not the usual answer

**Centrifugo has no user accounts.** No signup form, no install wizard, no first-visitor race.
The only privileged surface is the admin UI, and it is guarded by a password and a token-signing
secret that are set from environment variables before the container ever starts. That is the
deploy-time case, which is the only one that is safe by construction.

What that leaves you responsible for is the four secrets, since nothing on the server can
regenerate or recover them:

| Variable | What it protects |
|---|---|
| `CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | the admin web UI |
| `CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_SECRET` | the tokens that UI issues to itself |
| `CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY` | the server API your backend publishes through |
| `CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_TOKEN_HMAC_SECRET_KEY` | every connection JWT your backend signs |

## The compose to use

Upstream's `docker-compose.yml` is an integration-test harness of eight services and contains
no Centrifugo container at all, so it is not a starting point. This is:

```yaml
services:
  centrifugo:
    image: centrifugo/centrifugo:v6.9.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    environment:
      CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_SERVER_PORT: "8000"
      CENTRIFUGO_HEALTH_ENABLED: "true"
      CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_ENABLED: "true"
      CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_SECRET: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_INSECURE: "false"
      CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_INSECURE: "false"
      CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_INSECURE: "false"
      CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_TOKEN_HMAC_SECRET_KEY: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: "${CENTRIFUGO_ALLOWED_ORIGINS}"
      CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_CONNECT_WITHOUT_TOKEN: "[REDACTED:value]"
      CENTRIFUGO_LOG_LEVEL: "info"
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 65536
        hard: 65536
```

The four secret values go in the project `.env`, which you generate and hand to the user.
`CENTRIFUGO_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is a **space-separated** list of the origins your apps are served
from.

## Verify it, and prove the insecure flags are actually off

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify a Centrifugo deploy. Exit 0 pass, 1 fail, 3 inconclusive.
# Usage: ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] API_KEY=[REDACTED:value] ./verify.sh centrifugo-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
if [ "$#" -lt 1 ]; then
  echo "usage: ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] API_KEY=[REDACTED:value] $0 <centrifugo-host.redu.cloud>" >&2
  exit 2
fi
HOST=$1
INCONCLUSIVE=3
if [ -z "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" ] || [ -z "$API_KEY" ]; then
  echo "set ADMIN_PASSWORD and API_KEY in the environment, not on the command line" >&2
  exit 2
fi
TMP=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# (1) Is it Centrifugo answering, or redu's proxy while the container starts? /admin/init is the
# only endpoint that returns something nothing else could return.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/init" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/admin/init")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the container is still starting. Re-run shortly." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP $code on /admin/init. If it is 404, the admin UI is disabled." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if ! grep -qF '"edition"' "$TMP/init"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP 200 but the body is not a Centrifugo admin init response." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi

# (2) The security assertion, in the SAME body that just proved we are talking to Centrifugo,
# so it cannot go vacuous. insecure true means every admin endpoint is unauthenticated.
if grep -qF '"insecure":true' "$TMP/init"; then
  echo "FAIL: admin.insecure is ON. Every admin endpoint is open to the internet." >&2
  echo "Take this instance down now, unset CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_INSECURE and redeploy." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -qF '"insecure":false' "$TMP/init"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /admin/init reported neither insecure true nor false." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi

# (3) The admin password WORKS, not merely that it was set. Body in a file, never in argv.
printf 'password=[REDACTED:value]' "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" > "$TMP/body"
curl -sS -X POST -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary "@$TMP/body" "https://$HOST/admin/auth" > "$TMP/auth"
ADMIN_TOKEN=«REDACTED:assigned:6d257615» -o '"token":"[REDACTED:value]"]*"' "$TMP/auth" | cut -d'"' -f4)
if [ -z "$ADMIN_TOKEN" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: /admin/auth returned no token. A 400 here means the password or the secret is" >&2
  echo "empty; anything else means the password is wrong." >&2
  cat "$TMP/auth" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: admin login works."

# (4) The API key WORKS. The header goes in a curl config file, not in argv where ps shows it.
printf 'header = "X-API-Key: %s"' "$API_KEY" > "$TMP/curlrc"
withkey=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/info" -w '%{http_code}' -K "$TMP/curlrc" -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{}' "https://$HOST/api/info")
if [ "$withkey" = "404" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/info answered 404, so the route moved in this build and the check" >&2
  echo "below proves nothing. Do NOT leave this instance running until you re-verify by hand." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$withkey" != "200" ] || ! grep -qF '"result"' "$TMP/info"; then
  echo "FAIL: the API key did not work against /api/info (HTTP $withkey)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: the HTTP API accepts the key and /api/info returned a result."

# (5) Only NOW the negative: the same route must refuse an anonymous call. Step 4 is what makes
# this meaningful, because it already proved the route exists and is reachable.
nokey=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{}' "https://$HOST/api/info")
if [ "$nokey" != "401" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: /api/info answered $nokey without an API key, expected 401. The server API is" >&2
  echo "OPEN. Check CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY and CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_INSECURE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "OK: the API refuses an anonymous call (401), admin.insecure is off, and the admin"
echo "password and API key both work."
```

## The three that actually break it

**The empty origin list.** Leave `client.allowed_origins` unset and every browser handshake is
refused while server-side clients connect fine. The separator is a **space**, not a comma.

**The insecure flags.** `admin.insecure`, `http_api.insecure` and `client.insecure` each turn
off a whole authentication layer. They exist for a laptop. On a public hostname any one of them
is total compromise.

**The internal port.** Upstream tells you to split the admin UI and API onto a separate internal
port and firewall it. On redu that would put your control plane on a port nothing proxies. Leave
it unset, and let the API key and admin password do the work.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify a Centrifugo deploy. Exit 0 pass, 1 fail, 3 inconclusive.
# Usage: ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] API_KEY=[REDACTED:value] ./verify.sh centrifugo-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
if [ "$#" -lt 1 ]; then
  echo "usage: ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] API_KEY=[REDACTED:value] $0 <centrifugo-host.redu.cloud>" >&2
  exit 2
fi
HOST=$1
INCONCLUSIVE=3
if [ -z "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" ] || [ -z "$API_KEY" ]; then
  echo "set ADMIN_PASSWORD and API_KEY in the environment, not on the command line" >&2
  exit 2
fi
TMP=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# (1) Is it Centrifugo answering, or redu's proxy while the container starts? /admin/init is the
# only endpoint that returns something nothing else could return.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/init" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/admin/init")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the container is still starting. Re-run shortly." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP $code on /admin/init. If it is 404, the admin UI is disabled." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if ! grep -qF '"edition"' "$TMP/init"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP 200 but the body is not a Centrifugo admin init response." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi

# (2) The security assertion, in the SAME body that just proved we are talking to Centrifugo,
# so it cannot go vacuous. insecure true means every admin endpoint is unauthenticated.
if grep -qF '"insecure":true' "$TMP/init"; then
  echo "FAIL: admin.insecure is ON. Every admin endpoint is open to the internet." >&2
  echo "Take this instance down now, unset CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_INSECURE and redeploy." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -qF '"insecure":false' "$TMP/init"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /admin/init reported neither insecure true nor false." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi

# (3) The admin password WORKS, not merely that it was set. Body in a file, never in argv.
printf 'password=[REDACTED:value]' "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" > "$TMP/body"
curl -sS -X POST -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary "@$TMP/body" "https://$HOST/admin/auth" > "$TMP/auth"
ADMIN_TOKEN=«REDACTED:assigned:6d257615» -o '"token":"[REDACTED:value]"]*"' "$TMP/auth" | cut -d'"' -f4)
if [ -z "$ADMIN_TOKEN" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: /admin/auth returned no token. A 400 here means the password or the secret is" >&2
  echo "empty; anything else means the password is wrong." >&2
  cat "$TMP/auth" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: admin login works."

# (4) The API key WORKS. The header goes in a curl config file, not in argv where ps shows it.
printf 'header = "X-API-Key: %s"' "$API_KEY" > "$TMP/curlrc"
withkey=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/info" -w '%{http_code}' -K "$TMP/curlrc" -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{}' "https://$HOST/api/info")
if [ "$withkey" = "404" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/info answered 404, so the route moved in this build and the check" >&2
  echo "below proves nothing. Do NOT leave this instance running until you re-verify by hand." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$withkey" != "200" ] || ! grep -qF '"result"' "$TMP/info"; then
  echo "FAIL: the API key did not work against /api/info (HTTP $withkey)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: the HTTP API accepts the key and /api/info returned a result."

# (5) Only NOW the negative: the same route must refuse an anonymous call. Step 4 is what makes
# this meaningful, because it already proved the route exists and is reachable.
nokey=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{}' "https://$HOST/api/info")
if [ "$nokey" != "401" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: /api/info answered $nokey without an API key, expected 401. The server API is" >&2
  echo "OPEN. Check CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY and CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_INSECURE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "OK: the API refuses an anonymous call (401), admin.insecure is off, and the admin"
echo "password and API key both work."

  echo "Take this instance down now, unset CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_INSECURE and redeploy." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -qF '"insecure":false' "$TMP/init"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /admin/init reported neither insecure true nor false." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi

# (3) The admin password WORKS, not merely that it was set. Body in a file, never in argv.
printf 'password=[REDACTED:value]' "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" > "$TMP/body"
curl -sS -X POST -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary "@$TMP/body" "https://$HOST/admin/auth" > "$TMP/auth"
ADMIN_TOKEN=«REDACTED:assigned:6d257615» -o '"token":"[REDACTED:value]"]*"' "$TMP/auth" | cut -d'"' -f4)
if [ -z "$ADMIN_TOKEN" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: /admin/auth returned no token. A 400 here means the password or the secret is" >&2
  echo "empty; anything else means the password is wrong." >&2
  cat "$TMP/auth" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: admin login works."

# (4) The API key WORKS. The header goes in a curl config file, not in argv where ps shows it.
printf 'header = "X-API-Key: %s"' "$API_KEY" > "$TMP/curlrc"
withkey=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/info" -w '%{http_code}' -K "$TMP/curlrc" -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{}' "https://$HOST/api/info")
if [ "$withkey" = "404" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/info answered 404, so the route moved in this build and the check" >&2
  echo "below proves nothing. Do NOT leave this instance running until you re-verify by hand." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$withkey" != "200" ] || ! grep -qF '"result"' "$TMP/info"; then
  echo "FAIL: the API key did not work against /api/info (HTTP $withkey)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: the HTTP API accepts the key and /api/info returned a result."

# (5) Only NOW the negative: the same route must refuse an anonymous call. Step 4 is what makes
# this meaningful, because it already proved the route exists and is reachable.
nokey=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{}' "https://$HOST/api/info")
if [ "$nokey" != "401" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: /api/info answered $nokey without an API key, expected 401. The server API is" >&2
  echo "OPEN. Check CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY and CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_INSECURE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "OK: the API refuses an anonymous call (401), admin.insecure is off, and the admin"
echo "password and API key both work."

---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/centrifugal/centrifugo
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: centrifugo/centrifugo:v6.9.1
  port: 8000
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: none. Centrifugo's default engine is in-memory; do not provision one
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0174
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: centrifugo
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: NOBODY, BECAUSE CENTRIFUGO HAS NO USER ACCOUNTS AT ALL. There is no signup form, no install wizard and no first-visitor race, and that IS the ownership answer for this app. The only privileged surface is the admin web UI, and it is guarded by a single password plus a token-signing secret that YOU set at deploy time from environment variables (internal/configtypes/types.go:609-621). That is the deploy-time case, the one that is safe by construction. Two consequences: there is no window to close after boot, and there is also nobody to recover the password from, so record it with the user at handover."
  - "⛔⛔⛔ NEVER SET admin.insecure, http_api.insecure OR client.insecure ON A PUBLIC HOSTNAME, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT ENDS BADLY. internal/admin/handlers.go:62-70: when admin.insecure is true the auth middleware returns the handler UNWRAPPED, so every admin endpoint including POST /admin/api is open to the internet. /admin/api is the full server API: publish into any channel, disconnect any user, read history and presence. The equivalents are http_api.insecure (drops the API key check, internal/app/mux.go:259-260) and client.insecure (accepts every client connection as anonymous, internal/configtypes/types.go:471). All three exist for a laptop on localhost. Every tutorial that shows them is talking about a laptop. Leave all three FALSE, and never set client.token.insecure_skip_token_signature_verify either."
  - "⛔ SET admin.password AND admin.secret TOGETHER, OR THE UI IS DEAD RATHER THAN OPEN. Verified in internal/admin/handlers.go:73-77 and 139-143: an empty secret makes every admin request 401 with \"no admin secret key found in configuration\" in the log, and an empty password OR secret makes POST /admin/auth answer 400 with \"admin_password and admin_secret must be set in configuration\". So Centrifugo fails CLOSED, which is the good news, and the bad news is that it looks exactly like a broken deployment. Generate both (`openssl rand -hex 32` each), set CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_ENABLED, CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_SECRET, and prove the login works with the script in the body of this file rather than assuming."
  - "⛔ THE ADMIN UI, THE HTTP API AND HEALTH ARE ALL ON THE SAME PORT AS THE WEBSOCKET, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE HERE. internal/app/mux.go:390-393: if http_server.internal_port is empty, Centrifugo reuses the main port for the internal endpoints. Upstream's advice for a datacentre is to set a separate internal port and firewall it; on redu that would put the admin UI and the API on a port NOTHING proxies, and you would have deployed an unreachable control plane. So LEAVE internal_port UNSET, accept that /admin and /api are on the public hostname, and treat CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY and CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD as the only things standing between the internet and your message bus. Both fail closed when empty, but empty is not a security posture."
  - "⛔ SET client.allowed_origins OR EVERY BROWSER IS REFUSED WHILE EVERYTHING ELSE LOOKS FINE. internal/app/origin.go:16-26: with the list EMPTY, Centrifugo allows only requests that carry NO Origin header. Browsers always send one, so every browser WebSocket handshake is rejected and the only evidence is an info-level log line, \"request Origin is not authorized due to empty allowed_origins\". Server-side clients send no Origin and connect happily, which is what makes this look like the browser's fault. Set it to the exact origins of the apps that will connect. ⚠️ THE SEPARATOR IS A SPACE, NOT A COMMA (internal/config/envconfig/envconfig.go:270 sets SliceSep to a single space), so CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS should read like \"https://app.example.com https://staging.example.com\". A comma-separated value becomes ONE nonsense origin and every browser stays refused. Using * works and logs a warning; prefer the exact list."
  - "⛔ THE SECRETS ARE THE WHOLE PRODUCT, AND A REDEPLOY THAT REGENERATES THEM BREAKS YOUR BACKEND SILENTLY ON CENTRIFUGO'S SIDE. There is no database here, so nothing local is lost, and that is exactly why this is easy to miss: (1) CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_TOKEN_HMAC_SECRET_KEY verifies every connection JWT your backend mints (internal/configtypes/types.go:53-54). Change it and every existing token is rejected and every client fails to connect. (2) CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY is what your backend sends on every publish. Change it and every publish starts answering 401 while the realtime layer stays up, so your app looks alive and stops updating. (3) CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_SECRET signs admin sessions. Generate all three ONCE, store them with the user, and pass the SAME values on every redeploy."
  - "NO DATABASE. DO NOT PROVISION ONE. engine.type defaults to \"memory\" (internal/configtypes/engine.go:5), so a single-node Centrifugo keeps channel history and presence in RAM and needs nothing else. That is why this is the cheapest possible entry: one m1.small VM and no second machine on the bill. The honest cost of that default: history and presence are LOST on every restart and every redeploy, and you cannot run two Centrifugo nodes. Both are fixed the same way, by pointing engine.type at redis, which on redu means a managed Redis and roughly GBP 0.0174/hr more. That changes the quote, so it is the user's decision, not yours. Say it up front rather than after the first restart."
  - "PORT 8000, from internal/configtypes/types.go:18. Pass 8000 to deploy_compose. Health check: set CENTRIFUGO_HEALTH_ENABLED=true (it defaults to FALSE, internal/configtypes/types.go:375) and probe GET /health, which returns the literal two-character JSON body {} (internal/health/health.go:27-30). ⚠️ That body is a terrible thing to assert on by itself, since almost any JSON endpoint could produce it. Assert on GET /admin/init instead, which returns edition and insecure fields that only Centrifugo serves."
  - "⛔ DO NOT USE THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE. IT IS A TEST HARNESS AND IT DOES NOT CONTAIN CENTRIFUGO. centrifugal/centrifugo's docker-compose.yml starts nats, postgres, a streaming postgres replica that WIPES ITSELF on every restart (its own comment says so), a Google Pub/Sub emulator, localstack, redpanda, kafka and redis, all for integration tests against consumers. There is no centrifugo service in it. misc/clickhouse_cluster/docker-compose.yml is likewise for the PRO analytics feature. Write the one-service compose in the body of this file instead, pulling centrifugo/centrifugo:v6.9.1. Never :latest: the tag exists and a redeploy across a release would change the app under the user."
  - "CONFIGURE IT WITH ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES, NOT A CONFIG FILE, AND KNOW THE NAMING RULE. The image looks for ./config.json in /centrifugo and, not finding one, logs \"config file not found, continue using environment and flag options\" and carries on (internal/app/cmd.go:18, internal/app/run.go:66-67). That warning is EXPECTED with this recipe and is not an error. Env names are CENTRIFUGO_ plus the config path with dots replaced by underscores, uppercased: http_server.port becomes CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_SERVER_PORT, client.token.hmac_secret_key becomes CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_TOKEN_HMAC_SECRET_KEY, http_api.key becomes CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY. Note http_server, not http."
  - "A TYPO IN A VARIABLE NAME IS A WARNING, NOT A FAILURE, SO GREP FOR IT. internal/config/config.go:226 collects every CENTRIFUGO_* variable it does not recognise and internal/app/log.go:32-34 logs each as \"unknown var in environment\". Nothing fails. So a misspelled CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD leaves the admin UI unusable with no obvious cause. After boot check BOTH halves: `sudo docker logs <container> | grep -c 'starting Centrifugo'` must be at least 1, which is what proves your command reached the container at all, and only then `sudo docker logs <container> | grep 'unknown var in environment'` must be empty. A zero from the second grep means nothing unless the first one is non-zero."
  - "⛔ ANONYMOUS CONNECTIONS ARE OFF BY DEFAULT, KEEP THEM THAT WAY. client.allow_anonymous_connect_without_token defaults to false (internal/configtypes/types.go:428), so a client that presents no JWT is refused. That is correct: Centrifugo's entire authorisation model is the token your backend signs, which carries the user id and the channels they may subscribe to. Turning it on makes every channel that is not otherwise protected readable by anyone who can reach the hostname. If the user genuinely wants a public broadcast channel, that is a per-namespace decision in the channel config, not a global flag."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, with this recipe: GET / serves the admin single-page app, which is static assets and no data; GET /admin/init returns {\"insecure\":false,\"edition\":\"oss\",\"authenticated\":false} and nothing more; GET /health returns {}; POST /admin/api and POST /api both answer 401 without a token or key; and the WebSocket endpoint refuses a connection with no JWT. Nothing else is registered, because prometheus, swagger and the pprof debug handler all default to false (internal/configtypes/types.go:356, 380, 385) and this recipe leaves them there. Do not enable /metrics on the public port without thinking about what it exposes."
  - "NO VOLUME AND NO PERSISTENT STATE. The container writes nothing it needs to keep: no database, no uploads, no config file with this recipe. That makes a redeploy genuinely stateless, and it is also why the secrets above must be recorded outside the deployment. If you later switch to a config file, mount it read-only and remember the container runs as uid 1000 (Dockerfile, USER centrifugo)."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED, and no first-boot setup step at all. The binary starts and serves. That is unusual in this library and worth saying out loud: if the URL answers and the admin login works, the deploy is finished."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO NUMBER IN THE REPO. It is a single static Go binary on alpine with an in-memory broker, so m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is a reasonable floor and makes this the cheapest shape in the library at one VM and no database. ⚠️ The estimate is per-connection-count, not per-app: memory here scales with concurrent connections, their message queues (client.queue_max_size defaults to 1 MB per connection as a CEILING, not an allocation) and retained channel history. A few thousand idle connections is a different machine from a few hundred. Measure it on your run and write the real number back."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (GBP 0.0174/hr, about GBP 12.70 a month, NO managed database, inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), no database, port 8000. ⚠️ plan_deploy upsizes a compose stack to m1.large once needs_compose is declared; pass flavor_id explicitly to hold m1.small, because that larger floor exists for apps that BUILD from source and this one is a pulled static binary."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built. Write the one-service compose locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the Centrifugo repository would pick up the integration-test compose described above and start eight containers that have nothing to do with the app."
  - "WEBSOCKETS WORK THROUGH redu's PROXY, and you do not have to do anything to make that true: redu creates every proxy host with websocket upgrade enabled. Clients connect to wss://<your-host>/connection/websocket. If you want the SSE or HTTP-streaming fallbacks for networks that block WebSocket, they are separate handlers and both default to DISABLED (internal/configtypes/types.go:110, 117); enabling them also registers the /emulation endpoint automatically (internal/app/mux.go:418-421)."
  - "LICENCE: Apache 2.0, verified from the LICENSE file itself, 202 lines, Copyright 2023 Centrifugal Labs LTD, unmodified and with no network clause. ⚠️ awesome-selfhosted's metadata says MIT and is WRONG. Note also that Centrifugo PRO is a separate commercial product: the OSS build reports edition \"oss\" on /admin/init, and nothing in this recipe enables or requires PRO."
  - "DELETING IT TAKES EVERYTHING WITH IT, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF MOST ENTRIES HERE. There is no managed database left behind and no residual bill, because there was never a second machine. There is also no history to recover: with the memory engine, channel history and presence exist only in the running process. Say that plainly before deleting, and remember that every client and backend still pointed at the old hostname will simply stop connecting."
---

# Self-host Centrifugo on redu

A real-time messaging server you own: WebSocket connections, channels, presence and history, with
your backend publishing over an HTTP API. One small Go container, no database, and a public
HTTPS URL with TLS.

## What this deploys

- **Centrifugo** from the official image, pinned to `v6.9.1`, on one m1.small VM, port 8000.
- **No database.** The default engine keeps channel history and presence in memory, so there is
  nothing else to provision and nothing else on the bill.
- The admin web UI, the HTTP API and the WebSocket endpoint on one public hostname, with the
  admin password, the admin secret and the API key all set at deploy time.

GBP 0.0174/hour, about GBP 12.70 a month. The cheapest shape in this library, and inside the
no-card free trial.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Centrifugo on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## How ownership works here, because it is not the usual answer

**Centrifugo has no user accounts.** No signup form, no install wizard, no first-visitor race.
The only privileged surface is the admin UI, and it is guarded by a password and a token-signing
secret that are set from environment variables before the container ever starts. That is the
deploy-time case, which is the only one that is safe by construction.

What that leaves you responsible for is the four secrets, since nothing on the server can
regenerate or recover them:

| Variable | What it protects |
|---|---|
| `CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | the admin web UI |
| `CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_SECRET` | the tokens that UI issues to itself |
| `CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY` | the server API your backend publishes through |
| `CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_TOKEN_HMAC_SECRET_KEY` | every connection JWT your backend signs |

## The compose to use

Upstream's `docker-compose.yml` is an integration-test harness of eight services and contains
no Centrifugo container at all, so it is not a starting point. This is:

```yaml
services:
  centrifugo:
    image: centrifugo/centrifugo:v6.9.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    environment:
      CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_SERVER_PORT: "8000"
      CENTRIFUGO_HEALTH_ENABLED: "true"
      CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_ENABLED: "true"
      CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_SECRET: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_INSECURE: "false"
      CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_INSECURE: "false"
      CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_INSECURE: "false"
      CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_TOKEN_HMAC_SECRET_KEY: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: "${CENTRIFUGO_ALLOWED_ORIGINS}"
      CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_CONNECT_WITHOUT_TOKEN: "[REDACTED:value]"
      CENTRIFUGO_LOG_LEVEL: "info"
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 65536
        hard: 65536
```

The four secret values go in the project `.env`, which you generate and hand to the user.
`CENTRIFUGO_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is a **space-separated** list of the origins your apps are served
from.

## Verify it, and prove the insecure flags are actually off

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify a Centrifugo deploy. Exit 0 pass, 1 fail, 3 inconclusive.
# Usage: ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] API_KEY=[REDACTED:value] ./verify.sh centrifugo-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
if [ "$#" -lt 1 ]; then
  echo "usage: ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] API_KEY=[REDACTED:value] $0 <centrifugo-host.redu.cloud>" >&2
  exit 2
fi
HOST=$1
INCONCLUSIVE=3
if [ -z "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" ] || [ -z "$API_KEY" ]; then
  echo "set ADMIN_PASSWORD and API_KEY in the environment, not on the command line" >&2
  exit 2
fi
TMP=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# (1) Is it Centrifugo answering, or redu's proxy while the container starts? /admin/init is the
# only endpoint that returns something nothing else could return.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/init" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/admin/init")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the container is still starting. Re-run shortly." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP $code on /admin/init. If it is 404, the admin UI is disabled." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if ! grep -qF '"edition"' "$TMP/init"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP 200 but the body is not a Centrifugo admin init response." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi

# (2) The security assertion, in the SAME body that just proved we are talking to Centrifugo,
# so it cannot go vacuous. insecure true means every admin endpoint is unauthenticated.
if grep -qF '"insecure":true' "$TMP/init"; then
  echo "FAIL: admin.insecure is ON. Every admin endpoint is open to the internet." >&2
  echo "Take this instance down now, unset CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_INSECURE and redeploy." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -qF '"insecure":false' "$TMP/init"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /admin/init reported neither insecure true nor false." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi

# (3) The admin password WORKS, not merely that it was set. Body in a file, never in argv.
printf 'password=[REDACTED:value]' "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" > "$TMP/body"
curl -sS -X POST -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary "@$TMP/body" "https://$HOST/admin/auth" > "$TMP/auth"
ADMIN_TOKEN=«REDACTED:assigned:6d257615» -o '"token":"[REDACTED:value]"]*"' "$TMP/auth" | cut -d'"' -f4)
if [ -z "$ADMIN_TOKEN" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: /admin/auth returned no token. A 400 here means the password or the secret is" >&2
  echo "empty; anything else means the password is wrong." >&2
  cat "$TMP/auth" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: admin login works."

# (4) The API key WORKS. The header goes in a curl config file, not in argv where ps shows it.
printf 'header = "X-API-Key: %s"' "$API_KEY" > "$TMP/curlrc"
withkey=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/info" -w '%{http_code}' -K "$TMP/curlrc" -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{}' "https://$HOST/api/info")
if [ "$withkey" = "404" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/info answered 404, so the route moved in this build and the check" >&2
  echo "below proves nothing. Do NOT leave this instance running until you re-verify by hand." >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$withkey" != "200" ] || ! grep -qF '"result"' "$TMP/info"; then
  echo "FAIL: the API key did not work against /api/info (HTTP $withkey)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: the HTTP API accepts the key and /api/info returned a result."

# (5) Only NOW the negative: the same route must refuse an anonymous call. Step 4 is what makes
# this meaningful, because it already proved the route exists and is reachable.
nokey=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{}' "https://$HOST/api/info")
if [ "$nokey" != "401" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: /api/info answered $nokey without an API key, expected 401. The server API is" >&2
  echo "OPEN. Check CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY and CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_INSECURE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "OK: the API refuses an anonymous call (401), admin.insecure is off, and the admin"
echo "password and API key both work."
```

## The three that actually break it

**The empty origin list.** Leave `client.allowed_origins` unset and every browser handshake is
refused while server-side clients connect fine. The separator is a **space**, not a comma.

**The insecure flags.** `admin.insecure`, `http_api.insecure` and `client.insecure` each turn
off a whole authentication layer. They exist for a laptop. On a public hostname any one of them
is total compromise.

**The internal port.** Upstream tells you to split the admin UI and API onto a separate internal
port and firewall it. On redu that would put your control plane on a port nothing proxies. Leave
it unset, and let the API key and admin password do the work.
