lines: - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, with this recipe: GET / serves the admin single-page app, which is static assets and no data; GET /admin/init returns {\"insecure\":false,\"edition\":\"oss\",\"authenticated\":false} and nothing more; GET /health returns {}; POST /admin/api and POST /api both answer 401 without a token or key; and the WebSocket endpoint refuses a connection with no JWT. Nothing else is registered, because prometheus, swagger and the pprof debug handler all default to false (internal/configtypes/types.go:356, 380, 385) and this recipe leaves them there. Do not enable /metrics on the public port without thinking about what it exposes."

- "NO VOLUME AND NO PERSISTENT STATE. The container writes nothing it needs to keep: no database, no uploads, no config file with this recipe. That makes a redeploy genuinely stateless, and it is also why the secrets above must be recorded outside the deployment. If you later switch to a config file, mount it read-only and remember the container runs as uid 1000 (Dockerfile, USER centrifugo)."

- "NO migrate_command NEEDED, and no first-boot setup step at all. The binary starts and serves. That is unusual in this library and worth saying out loud: if the URL answers and the admin login works, the deploy is finished."

-  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO NUMBER IN THE REPO. It is a single static Go binary on alpine with an in-memory broker, so m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is a reasonable floor and makes this the cheapest shape in the library at one VM and no database. ⚠️ The estimate is per-connection-count, not per-app: memory here scales with concurrent connections, their message queues (client.queue_max_size defaults to 1 MB per connection as a CEILING, not an allocation) and retained channel history. A few thousand idle connections is a different machine from a few hundred. Measure it on your run and write the real number back."

+  - "SIZING, NOW MEASURED ON DEPLOY #442: the container idles at 26.85 MiB of the VM's 1.922 GiB (docker stats, zero connections), and the whole VM sits at 429 MB of 1967 MB with Docker and the OS included. So m1.small is not merely a reasonable floor, it is roughly 70x headroom AT IDLE, and the deploy went ready in about 5 minutes with no restarts. ⚠️ That number is per-connection-count, not per-app, and it is the idle figure: memory scales with concurrent connections, their message queues (client.queue_max_size defaults to 1 MB per connection as a CEILING, not an allocation) and retained channel history. A few thousand idle connections is a different machine from a few hundred. Re-measure at YOUR load before trusting 26 MB."

+  - "⛔ PIN THE dname BEFORE YOU DEPLOY, BECAUSE allowed_origins NEEDS THE URL THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET. This is a chicken-and-egg unique to this app: CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS wants exact origins, and if the Centrifugo host itself is one of them you cannot know it until after the deploy, at which point the container has already booted with the wrong list. Generate the FULL auto-gen form yourself — `centrifugo-<8 lowercase letters/digits>.redu.cloud`, e.g. via `tr -dc 'a-z0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 8` — and pass it as deploy_compose's dname, which uses it VERBATIM. ⚠️ A BARE `centrifugo.redu.cloud` does NOT work for this: redu appends its own random 8-char suffix, so the origin you baked into the env would never match the real URL and every browser would be refused."

+  - "SECRETS REACH THE VM VIA deploy_compose's env PARAMETER, NOT VIA A LOCAL .env. prepare_upload deliberately EXCLUDES .env from the tarball, so the four secrets have to be passed as the `env` argument to deploy_compose, which appends them to the project .env on the VM. The compose file references them as ${CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD} etc, and note the two names that do NOT match their config key: the .env keys are CENTRIFUGO_TOKEN_HMAC_SECRET_KEY and CENTRIFUGO_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, which feed the longer CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_TOKEN_HMAC_SECRET_KEY and CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS container variables. On the VM that file is 0600 root-only: read it with `sudo cat /opt/app-src/.env`."

+  - "THE CONTAINER IS NAMED app-src-centrifugo-1, AND THE VM RUNS DOCKER, NOT PODMAN. redu names the compose project app-src regardless of what you called the deployment, so the grep-for-typos check above is literally `sudo docker logs app-src-centrifugo-1 | grep -c 'starting Centrifugo'` (must be >=1) then `... | grep 'unknown var in environment'` (must be empty). Verified on #442: 1 and empty. The ONLY log line at boot was the expected \"config file not found, continue using environment and flag options\" warning."

+  - "plan_deploy QUOTED m1.large AT GBP 35.48/mo ON THIS RECIPE, MEASURED ON #442, which is 2.8x the real GBP 12.70. It cannot see that the image is PULLED rather than built, so declaring needs_compose triggers its build-capable floor. Passing flavor_id '2' held m1.small and the deploy was fine. Show the user the real number, not plan_deploy's."

- "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (GBP 0.0174/hr, about GBP 12.70 a month, NO managed database, inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), no database, port 8000. ⚠️ plan_deploy upsizes a compose stack to m1.large once needs_compose is declared; pass flavor_id explicitly to hold m1.small, because that larger floor exists for apps that BUILD from source and this one is a pulled static binary."

- "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built. Write the one-service compose locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the Centrifugo repository would pick up the integration-test compose described above and start eight containers that have nothing to do with the app."

- "WEBSOCKETS WORK THROUGH redu's PROXY, and you do not have to do anything to make that true: redu creates every proxy host with websocket upgrade enabled. Clients connect to wss://<your-host>/connection/websocket. If you want the SSE or HTTP-streaming fallbacks for networks that block WebSocket, they are separate handlers and both default to DISABLED (internal/configtypes/types.go:110, 117); enabling them also registers the /emulation endpoint automatically (internal/app/mux.go:418-421)."

Centrifugo is live and verified.

**https://centrifugo-w9il598w.redu.cloud** — deployment `442`, m1.small, **GBP 0.0174/hr (~GBP 12.70/mo)**, no database.

## Verified, not assumed

`verify.sh` exited 0 against the live host:

- `/admin/init` returns `"edition"` and **`"insecure":false`** — Centrifugo is answering, and `admin.insecure` is off
- `POST /admin/auth` returns a token — password *and* secret both work
- `POST /api/info` with the key returns a result; **401 without it** — the server API is closed

On the VM, both halves of the typo check pass: `starting Centrifugo` = 1 (the env actually reached the container) and `unknown var in environment` is empty (no variable name was misspelled). The only boot warning is the expected `config file not found`.

Measured: the container idles at **26.85 MiB** of 1.92 GiB, zero restarts, `centrifugo/centrifugo:v6.9.1`.

## Your four secrets

Written to `.env` (mode 0600, never uploaded, never in `redu.md`). Nothing on the server can recover them — store them somewhere durable, and pass the *same* values on every redeploy:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | `«REDACTED:longhex:ed7222c4»` |
| `CENTRIFUGO_ADMIN_SECRET` | `«REDACTED:longhex:8ba79cba»` |
| `CENTRIFUGO_HTTP_API_KEY` | `«REDACTED:longhex:ef805257»` |
| `CENTRIFUGO_CLIENT_TOKEN_HMAC_SECRET_KEY` | `«REDACTED:longhex:8f2ab8ac»` |

Log in at the URL with the admin password. Clients connect to `wss://centrifugo-w9il598w.redu.cloud/connection/websocket`; your backend publishes to `/api` with `X-API-Key`.

## Two things to know

**Allowed origins is currently just the Centrifugo host.** Server-side clients connect fine (no `Origin` header), but a browser app served from anywhere else will be refused with only an info-level log line as evidence. Tell me the origins and I'll redeploy with them — space-separated, and it must be the same secrets.

**No persistence.** Channel history and presence live only in the running process, so they're lost on restart and you can't run a second node. Managed Redis fixes both at roughly double the bill.

## Files written

- `redu.md` — added the pinned `dname`, the `last_deploy` block, the real deploy-log entry, and **5 new quirks** this run taught (the sizing quirk now carries the measured 26.85 MiB instead of an estimate; plan_deploy's m1.large over-quote is now recorded as measured at 2.8x; and the `dname` chicken-and-egg — `allowed_origins` needs a URL that doesn't exist until after deploy, so the subdomain must be generated up front). The server-side merge was withheld (21,622 chars, over its 24,000 budget), so I applied its two edits by hand as instructed and typed the quirks myself.
- `redu-deploy-plan.md` — replaced with the real provisioned values
- `docker-compose.yml`, `verify.sh` — the one-service compose and the verification script
- `.env` — the secrets, 0600
